messages.subject: Re: Compare IRF of GRM (mirt-package) with nonparametric IRF from KernsmoothIRT?
parts:
The packages use very different graphical systems (lattice vs graphics), so in general merging information will be difficult. You will likely need to extract the core information from one (or both) package(s) and render the plot yourself (mirt has some low-level extractor functions, like probtrace(), which may be helpful in this situation). I'm sure if this will always work for these IRT packages since scaling/identification parameterization differences could exist, so more work may be needed before superimposing the tracelines onto the same graphical space.

Phil


On Tue, Mar 16, 2021 at 9:47 AM Barbara Meier <johanna...@gmx.net> wrote:

Hello!

Is there a way to generate one single plot, which graphically compares the IRF-function of the unidimensional graded response model with the nonparametric IRF-function?
I managed to get comparable graphics out of mirt and KernSmooth-IRT, but I can't figure out a way to combine these to plots into one?
Can anyone help me with that?

library(KernSmoothIRT)
data(BDI)
GRM<- mirt(data=BDIresponses, model= 1, itemtype="graded") ; GRM
ks.IRT<-ksIRT(data.frame(BDIresponses), format = 2, key=4)


plot(ks.IRT, plottype="EIS", item=1, axistype="distribution", main="", xlab="Expected Trait Score")
itemplot(GRM, item=1, type="score", xlim=c(-3.5,3.5))
